content:
I have noticed a bad merge of my PR TauCetiProject/TauCeti#4368 due to review/merge race (I have opened a refactor PR to address it, still in draft), I believe this is what happened:

  1. the eventually merged commit cd85e814 addressed change requests from CBirkbeck's codex reviewer but the commit had defects;
  2. kbuzzard's Claude reviewer held the review claim for 36 minutes and posted 7 correct change requests;
  3. during 2, utensil's codex review worker took the review claim after the 30 minute lease expired (see TauCetiReview/runner/cli.py for default lease of 1,800 seconds);
  4. utensil's codex review worker worked in reactivation mode, and "focused on whether those earlier localized defects had been repaired", thus given an all-green scoreboard (edit-in-place);
  5. the tauceti-review-bot added my PR into merge queue after seeing 4 (which is edited later than 2, making it a all-green latest review conclusion), even though my PR codex saw 2 too and addressed it in a new commit and pushed seconds before the old head cd85e814 is added to merge queue.

2 improvements I see:

  1. reviewer may claim a review after lease expires, but should abort posting or reconcile if other review comments were posted in between;
  2. tauceti-review-bot should handle review race somehow

One more thing worth discussing: reactivation mode could be used to clear earlier findings (or not, or partially), but maybe a full review should be run before merge.

Locally I also suffered from such tunnel-vision style review before so I runs full 2+1 review before opening a PR, however I don't run additional full review before pushing commits addressing change requests :joy: .
